story.text: Narrative Walks turns a published graph snapshot into enumerated paths through concepts, pages, or paragraph-level nodes. It reads `SOURCE graph` from the lineup (via Frame integration), indexes nodes and typed relations, and computes either (a) **all walks** (all directed simple paths, including single-node walks) or (b) **basis walks** (maximal source→sink paths under the chosen edge-type filter). Use this page to confirm that some upstream producer is publishing under topic `graph`, to inspect available edge types, and to export walk sets as FedWiki plain text for downstream work (claim templates, topic maps, reading paths, or comparative “[[Side Road]]” analysis).

How it works (overview)

1. Provide a graph snapshot
   A producer (plugin or frame) publishes graph source data under topic `graph`. The snapshot is JSONL containing a `{nodes:[...], rels:[...]}` payload.

2. Index nodes and relations
   Nodes are identified by array index; node labels default to `node.type` (falling back to `id`/index). Relations are directed edges with an optional `type`.

3. Compute walks
   Two modes are supported:

* All walks: enumerate directed simple paths up to a max-length cap (cycle-safe via “no node revisits”).
* Basis walks: enumerate maximal paths (typically source→sink) under the same edge filter.

4. Export
   Exports a FedWiki-ready, plain-text section listing the computed walks, suitable for copy/paste into analysis pages.

Minimal example

A directed chain with eight nodes (N1→N2→…→N8) contains 36 distinct directed paths (every contiguous forward segment). More generally, a directed chain of length *n* contains *n·(n+1)/2* walks in “all walks” mode.

item.text: Narrative Walks turns a published graph into enumerated paths through concepts. It reads SOURCE graph from the lineup (via the Frame integration), indexes nodes and typed relations, and then computes either (a) all narrative walks (all directed simple paths, including single-node walks) or (b) basis walks (maximal source→sink paths). Use this page to verify that a graph-producing plugin is publishing under topic graph, to inspect edge types, and to export walk sets in FedWiki plain text for downstream analysis (claim templates, topic maps, or reading-path documents).

Below is a concrete “topics → narrative walks” computation for an excerpt from Hannah Arendt, Was heißt persönliche Verantwortung in einer Diktatur?, treated as a **directed acyclic topic graph** (a minimal instance of the “narrative walk” idea: a walk is any directed path that follows the available edges, without repeating nodes). The first paragraph is quoted/discussed in Falkenhagen’s dissertation, with Arendt-reference “PV, S.44”.  The second paragraph is explicitly cited (as a German translation) in Arendt’s *Denktagebuch* apparatus (Kant-Heft note pointing to “Personal Responsibility Under Dictatorship”).

The first paragraph is quoted/discussed in Falkenhagen’s dissertation, with Arendt-reference “PV, S.44”.  The second paragraph is explicitly cited (as a German translation) in Arendt’s *Denktagebuch* apparatus (Kant-Heft note pointing to “Personal Responsibility Under Dictatorship”).

## 1) Topic nodes (8)

N1 **Value-codes are unreliable under moral collapse** (what remains is “habit of holding on to something”). 
N2 **Skeptics/doubters are more reliable** (because they habitually check, form their own judgment). 
N3 **Best are those who know they must live with themselves** (inner cohabitation constraint). 

N4 **Objection: are non-participants “irresponsible”?** 
N5 **Extreme cases exist where one cannot assume responsibility for the world** (world as political entity). 
N6 **Political responsibility presupposes minimal political power** → **powerlessness is an excuse.** 
N7 **Admitting powerlessness requires a moral quality** (good will; reality-facing; no illusions). 
N8 **This admission preserves a residual strength/power even in desperate conditions.** 

## 2) Edges (minimal, as given by the text order)

N1 → N2 → N3 → N4 → N5 → N6 → N7 → N8

(One directed line; no branching edges were asserted in the excerpt itself.)

## 3) All possible narrative walks (all directed paths)

In a directed chain of length 8, the number of distinct directed paths is:

* **8·9/2 = 36** narrative walks (every contiguous forward segment).
